found: A correct selection was called wrong while the needle was still travelling to 15.
fix: Judge the gauge only once the needle has stopped (five readings over 5 s) and give the crew 5 s to move the lever.

found: In repeat runs a needle still creeping towards 15 was taken as settled: one false “ten set” in 9 runs.
fix: A trend test: the needle must not be moving. 9/9 since.

found: With live speech, clearance plus readback take ~12 s, so a correctly set MCP could be flagged before the crew had finished reading back.
fix: The grace period starts at the readback.

found: The first hand-height threshold flagged 3 of 6 normal images from three held-out image sets.
fix: Re-derived from the first set alone and tested on two sets made afterwards: 8/8 (24/24 over all six).

found: Two recordings captured another window in front of the simulator.
fix: Runs with an unreadable panel or a bright, non-cockpit frame are rejected, not scored.

found: Spark’s readings arrive 3.5–5 s after the frame is taken, so its callout came after speed was already 10 kt low: 0 of 4 runs in time.
fix: Call on the speed trend (where speed will be in 10 s, like the PFD’s trend arrow), with each reading timed at capture and applied the moment it arrives. Then in time in 6 of 6 fresh runs; over later runs 5 of 8. Spark is too slow for this alert about a third of the time; the on-device reader was in time in every run.

found: Over all its runs Spark was in time in 6 of 11. Reading the whole display took 4.6–5.4 s, most of it Spark thinking (966 prompt and 280–450 completion tokens), and this alert needs a fresh reading every two or three seconds.
fix: On final Spark reads the final lane, as Glimmer does on board: the selected speed, the speed box and the thrust and pitch mode boxes, the answer one line in a strict schema (median 2.2 s on recorded frames; airspeed 58 of 61, thrust 24 of 24). Saying that the white ARM is not a mode took the median from 3.9 s. Some reads still take 4–7 s, so a read starts every half second, up to 16 in flight. Two batches before the last found the rest: an older whole read arriving last could replace a newer selected altitude (now ignored, tested; the speeds were never affected, 6 of 6), and at one read a second one run waited 4.3 s for a reading and was late (5 of 6). In time in 7 of 7 fresh runs, 8.5–12.5 s after the fault and 1.9–3.9 s before speed was 10 kt low.

found: One misread altitude (918 ft while at 6,000) made Crosscheck think it was on final and raise the autothrottle alert.
fix: The phase comes from the median of the last three altitude readings.

found: A level-change descent (thrust at idle, the elevator holding speed) was read as “autothrottle not in speed”, twice.
fix: No alert while the pitch mode is holding speed.

found: The thrust-mode cell blanked for one frame during a mode change.
fix: The thrust and pitch modes must agree over consecutive readings.

found: On-device text recognition missed a plain “MCP SPD” on two frames in a row.
fix: Three readings in a row are required.

found: The readback “descend and maintain 4,000 LAS for 421” was dropped (“for” joined the callsign into 4421), and with no readback heard the MCP check fired 1 s before the crew set it.
fix: The callsign is also matched in the raw transcript; with no readback heard, the crew gets 15 s.

found: Spark’s readings arrive ~3.5 s after the frame; the crew set 11,000 at 26 s, Spark’s readings of it arrived from 33 s, and the 8 s grace had run out by the clock: a false “set niner thousand”.
fix: The grace is counted to the newest selector reading, not the clock, and Spark’s facts carry their capture time.

found: Voice Transcribe heard “climb and maintain one one thousand” as “climb and maintain 1000”, at 9,000 ft, in 3 runs in a row (and correctly in the others). In the first, Crosscheck flagged the correct readback against it; in the next two the guard below rejected it, leaving nothing to check: the bust and the readback error went uncalled. Once it heard a correct readback as \u201cmaintained 1000\u201d, adding a wrong readback callout to a caught bust.
fix: A climb to below the aircraft, or a descent to above it, is rejected as misheard and logged, and Crosscheck says “Confirm cleared altitude.” The two missed runs are counted as failures in the test matrix. The scorer now counts any unexpected callout as a wrong run. Since the last of these, a line whose value contradicts the aircraft is sent to Voice Transcribe a second time (“listen again”); it has not been needed in the runs since.

found: The misheard-number guard itself rejected a correct \u201cclimb and maintain 11000\u201d, because one altitude reading was misread as 68,193 ft at 9,000.
fix: The guard uses the median of the last three altitude readings, like the flight phase.

found: Spark was slow (readings 6–9 s after capture); four readings of the moving needle arrived together, looked settled at 5 when stamped on arrival, and Crosscheck said “five set” for 10.
fix: The flap facts carry their capture time, as the autothrottle’s do. Replayed that way, every recorded flaps run is right, this one included (“ten set”).

found: After the X-Plane demo’s 60 minutes the flight controls stop responding while the screen keeps drawing; two runs were invalid.
fix: The time-out dialog is recognised and X-Plane is restarted before the next run.

found: A laptop webcam sees only head and chest: neither measure told a slump from reading a checklist.
fix: The pilot watch needs a camera that sees the upper body and hands, as on a glareshield mount; it is tested on footage from that angle.

found: Neither open recognizer is good enough alone on the scenarios' lines: SeamlessM4T v2 dropped 15 of 51 values (it rewrote “flaps one” as “One of the flaps.”), Omnilingual ASR heard “maintain won one thousand” for one one thousand.
fix: Both hear every line; a value that contradicts the aircraft is dropped, then a value counts only when the two do not disagree. “Won” before a number is read as one, as “for” already was. 48 of 51 right, none wrong.

found: Asked for the needle’s clock position, Muse Glimmer was right on 8 of 20 frames; asked which marking, 20 of 20 on the shipped frames, but in live runs it read a needle parked at 5 as 2 on 4 of 22 frames, so the settle check never settled (2 of 3 “not moved” runs missed).
fix: Each marking’s place on the dial is in the question (19 of 20 shipped frames at 2x zoom; 3x read better but too slowly for the settle check to see five readings).

found: On the test computer X-Plane uses about 85% of the GPU, and a Glimmer read took 7 s; most of it was writing the answer.
fix: The answer is one short line instead of a JSON object per value (24 tokens, not 49) and the image is the three parts of the PFD the rules use: 4.4 s, same accuracy.

found: Without a JSON schema, Muse Glimmer spent its whole token budget and returned no text.
fix: The sentence under a callout is asked for as {“sentence”: …}, like every other Glimmer call.

found: On board the callout came 23–39 s after the fault, after speed was 10 kt low (6 runs). Two reads in flight on a busy GPU doubled each read’s delay to 9 s; the rule waited for three readings in a row (10 s at one every 5 s); an empty thrust box was sometimes left out of the answer, which lost the whole reading; and a few frames had the speed misread.
fix: One read in flight; on final two reads in three are only the speed tape and the mode boxes; two readings at least 3 s apart count like three in a row (both tested); the modes are asked for as a list of exactly three 737 mode names. Each read was then right on the frames it missed, but at one every 4–6 s still too late: 0 of 4.

found: Where the time went, read by read: a reading every 5.5 s, of which 0.6 s was the screenshot (a full-screen PNG written and read back) and the rest the read; one read in three or five was the whole set of parts (3.4–5.7 s), which could start just before the fault; and a whole read once took the selected speed for the speed.
fix: On final a final lane: the selected speed, the speed box and the thrust and pitch mode boxes, the answer one short string held to a pattern (each mode box only its own column’s modes): 2.15 s a read with X-Plane flying, as accurate as the fast lane on 61 recorded frames (airspeed 59 against 58, selected speed and thrust mode all right). The screen straight from the display, 0.08 s, the same pixels. A whole read at most every 30 s on final, none while the thrust box shows the autothrottle out of speed. A reading every 2.6 s; in time in 4 of 4 fresh runs, 9.5–14.5 s after the fault.

found: The flap scenario passed only one recognizer’s transcript, which had “fifteen flaps” backwards; the fallback then tried Muse Spark, and the sandbox refused the connection. 2 runs missed.
fix: It passes both transcripts like the other scenarios, and on board the second reader is always the local Glimmer.

found: Four false callouts in the first on-board flight. Three were one reading of the selector: with one read every ~5 s, the newest reading showed the crew’s new setting (or a stale read of the old one) while the vote still held the old value. One followed a clearance both recognizers missed: its readback was heard and compared with the clearance before.
fix: No callout while the newest reading disagrees with the vote; at least two readings after the readback must show the wrong setting; and a readback that answers a clearance Crosscheck did not hear means the cleared altitude is unknown, not the old one (three rules, each tested). All recordings replay unchanged.

found: Crosscheck’s own callouts in MMS-TTS, played to Muse Voice Transcribe, came back as “Fleered one 1000” and “flats 15 cult”.
fix: Callouts come from a recorded bank, as an aircraft’s aural alerts do (voice/bank.py): nine callouts, two passes each, 15 of 18 came back word for word, against 2 of 18 for MMS-TTS.

found: Voice Transcribe heard the radio-filtered “Portland altimeter three zero one two” as “Portland altitude 3012”, and the readback’s “altimeter” as “autometer”, so the setting was never in the ledger and Crosscheck stayed silent on a wrong setting.
fix: Those spellings count as “altimeter”; “altitude” only with a number that cannot be an altitude (altitudes are whole hundreds, 3012 is not). Tested on the two transcripts.

found: This 737 keeps its altimeter setting from one flight to the next and ignores X-Plane’s reset to 29.92, so runs began at 30.21 from the run before; the scorer counted the rule firing, not its words, and passed three runs that said the wrong number.
fix: Each run turns the knob back to 29.92 and stops if it is not there; the crew turns it a click at a time; the scorer requires the exact words for the variant. The six runs are kept as evidence, not counted.

found: Replaying the altimeter recording added a “Confirm cleared altitude.” the live run never said: just before the clearance, on-device text recognition misread the altitude three frames in a row (18,999, 605, 6,106 ft at 9,000), and the guard took the median of the last three readings, 6,106 ft, so “descend and maintain 7000” looked like a climb.
fix: The guard takes the median of the last five readings. Every recording replays exactly as it ran, this one included.

found: One run of the setting not made stayed silent: Voice Transcribe heard “Portland altimeter three zero one two” as “Portland diameter three zero one two”, so the setting ATC gave never reached the ledger.
fix: Kept as a miss. The readback (“autometer 3012”) was heard; using it when ATC's line is not understood is the next change, not yet tested.
